beats.purpose: Hook the viewer with the everyday mystery of how a small ground receiver pinpoints its position using signals sent from orbit.
beats.visual_intent: A smartphone on Earth receiving radio signals from an orbital constellation of satellites.

beats.purpose: Introduce the foundational mechanism of calculating distance by timing radio wave transmission at the speed of light.
beats.visual_intent: Synchronized radio waves carrying timestamps pulsing from an orbital satellite to a ground receiver.

beats.purpose: Demonstrate that overlapping distance spheres in three dimensions still leave an unknown receiver clock bias.
beats.visual_intent: Three intersecting 3D spheres centered on satellites narrowing location to two points, with a shifting receiver clock offset.

beats.purpose: Show how the fourth satellite eliminates clock error and locks in the precise three-dimensional coordinate.
beats.visual_intent: A fourth sphere converging with the intersection, collapsing the uncertainty to a single precise point on the surface.

output.rationale: The subject addresses a familiar everyday wonder—how a phone precisely locates itself on Earth using signals from space. A question-led arc allows us to establish the core distance-measuring mechanism intuitively, introduce the geometric and timing puzzle, and then resolve it cleanly with the four-satellite requirement.
output.title: How GPS Pinpoints Your Exact Location
